blindSummary: This state/province applies religious criminal law as part of the twelve-jurisdiction bloc. The parallel religious courts hold criminal jurisdiction over defendants of the locally dominant faith and criminalise same-sex conduct beyond the federal statute, including acts between women. No trans-specific incident, morality-police action, or case-level study data exists for this state/province in the record. The framework's presence and operational status since 2002 is the finding: an adherent - or a person perceived to adhere - of the locally dominant faith facing charges would answer before the parallel religious courts rather than a secular magistrate, under capital-capable statutes.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's report (2004), chapter on the extension of religious criminal law: the first jurisdiction in the bloc re-adopted religious criminal law (establishment statute enacted 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000); by 2002 twelve jurisdictions - this state/province among them - had religious criminal legislation and religious courts with criminal jurisdiction over adherents of the locally dominant faith, the only jurisdictions with such jurisdiction.
